summary:
Project Alphecca is an offline-ready Progressive Web App (PWA) designed to help smallholder farmers adapt to shifting climate conditions using NASA Earth observation data. By answering three simple questions—location, basic field/water resources, and farming goals—users receive a science-backed, multi-year crop rotation plan in seconds.
Powered by a FastAPI backend, the platform integrates NASA POWER historical climate data (2001–present), soil moisture, and soil temperature proxies with a transparent, 9-factor deterministic agronomy rule engine. It scores 21 crops, generates a 2-to-4-year family-diverse crop rotation timeline, grades soil health (A–D), and calculates seasonal water deficits in practical farmer units (tons per decare).
To prevent AI hallucinations, the rule engine strictly locks crop rankings, while an optional LLM layer translates technical outputs into plain-language steps. Built with large touch targets, high contrast, voice readout, and offline caching, Tarla Dostu bridges space data with everyday field decisions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Project Alphecca is an offline-ready Progressive Web App (PWA) designed to help smallholder farmers adapt their crop choices and multi-year rotations to shifting climate conditions. Users answer three simple questions: their field location (via an interactive map, GPS, or quick provincial presets), basic field and water conditions (area in decares, soil texture, pH, irrigation level), and their primary farming goal (yield, profit, low water use, or soil health).

In a single request, our FastAPI backend queries NASA POWER historical climate data (2001–present) alongside soil moisture and soil temperature proxies. A transparent, 9-factor deterministic agronomy rule engine then evaluates 21 crops across water balance (24%), temperature suitability (20%), farmer goals (14%), pH, salinity, and climate risk. Based on these scores, the system builds a 2-to-4-year crop rotation plan that prevents consecutive planting of the same plant family, grades soil health (A–D) across nine indicators, and calculates monthly water deficits in practical farmer units (tons per decare and m³).

Creativity & Human-Centered Factors Considered

  • Zero-Hallucination Hybrid AI: Instead of letting LLMs guess agricultural advice, our deterministic rule engine locks all scientific rankings. Interchangeable LLMs (Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, Groq, or local Ollama) are strictly used as a plain-language translation layer to generate easy-to-follow action checklists—with a keyless heuristic fallback when offline or without an API key.
  • Inclusive Accessibility: Built specifically for rural environments and low-literacy users, the interface features oversized touch targets, high-contrast modes, local-language text-to-speech (Voice Readout), and service-worker caching so farmers can view their saved plans in the field without internet access.
  • Scientific Honesty: Because NASA POWER does not provide field-level soil nutrients (N-P-K) or pH, our API explicitly flags missing inputs under data_gaps and clearly distinguishes historical climate trends from future forecasts.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Tarla Dostu turns complex space-grade Earth observation data into immediate, actionable field guidance. By promoting legume and root-depth diversity and highlighting exact seasonal water deficits, it reduces irrigation waste, restores soil organic health, and protects farmer livelihoods against climate volatility.

Tools, Languages & Tech Stack

  • Backend & Agronomy Engine: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn, Pytest (automated unit & mock-API testing), Docker.
  • Frontend (Farmer PWA): Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Service Workers (sw.js), Web Speech API (TTS), Leaflet.js.
  • Data & AI Integration: NASA POWER API, OpenStreetMap & Nominatim Reverse Geocoding, multi-provider LLM abstraction layer (heuristic fallback + Gemini/OpenAI/Anthropic/Ollama).
